claim: LLサイズ and XLサイズ both answer 'Size XL', and nothing on either back tells the learner that LL is the Japanese label for extra large, so one of the two cards looks like a mistake.
evidence: Reading front 'LLサイズ', back 'Answer: Size XL / Says: eru eru saizu'. Reading front 'XLサイズ' (r-09614a66bafb), back 'Answer: Size XL / Says: ekkusu eru saizu'. Neither card has a note.
fix: Add a note on LLサイズ saying LL is how Japanese shops label the size above L, the same as XL.
verdictReason: Preflight already reports this pair (reading-distinct-english, LLサイズ+XLサイズ "Size XL") and the owner accepted it on 2026-10-14; the book itself prints "LL サイズ／ XL サイズ (size XL)" (Lesson 5 table), so the card is faithful; and a reading card has no note field (docs/card-rules-reading.md: no scene, hint or note), so the proposed fix has nowhere to go.

claim: The romaji puts an apostrophe after ん before w, which the deck's own romanization never does elsewhere (こんばんは is 'konbanwa' with none).
evidence: Reading back 'Answer: Golden Week / Says: gōruden'wīku'. Same unit: 'こんばんは' says 'konbanwa', 'こんにちは' says 'konnichiwa'.
verdictReason: The cited evidence is wrong (こんばんは has no vowel after ん, and the deck DOES use apostrophes: kon'iro, sen'en, kin'yōbi, kon'ya, shin'yū, ten'in elsewhere in the collection) but the claim holds: the house style (src/translate/romajiStyle.js, rule n-apostrophe) puts an apostrophe only before a vowel or y, and gōruden'wīku is the only n' before w in the whole collection. Fix stands: gōrudenwīku.

claim: さん is carded as "Three" only, though the book also teaches 〜さん as "Mr./Ms." and both meanings fed this one card.
evidence: Book ch2 Numbers: "3 さん san". Book ch3 Lesson 1 vocabulary: "〜さん . . . san Mr./Ms. . . ." (the chapter-2 kanaPool holds さん "Mr; Ms"). Card r-0d0fd2531ac7: target さん, English "Three".
fix: Make the English "Three; Mr./Ms. (after a name)" so one written form carries both meanings the book teaches.
verdictReason: Book ch2 prints "3 さん san" and ch3 (Lesson 1 vocabulary) "〜さん Mr./Ms."; both reached the pool (reading-report.json: chapter-1 さん "Three", chapter-2 さん "Mr; Ms"), and src/reading/soundDeck.js dedups the pool with seen.has(entry.target), keeping the first entry and silently dropping the second's English, so rule 3 (one written form, English carries both meanings) was never applied. The deck already cards a bare suffix (じん "...people (nationality)"). No other さん card exists in the collection. Kept should-fix: さん as a title follows a proper name (never carded) on almost every page, so the learner has to read it alone.

claim: ご is carded as "Five" only, though the book also teaches 〜ご ". . . language", and the deck cards the sibling suffixes じん and ねんせい with their meanings.
evidence: Book ch2: "5 ご go". Book ch3 Lesson 1 vocabulary: "*〜ご . . . go . . . language" (chapter-2 kanaPool: ご "...language"). Card r-27a87259d93f: ご "Five"; compare r-a6f2cd3984e4 じん "...people (nationality)".
verdictReason: Same mechanism as さん: book ch2 "5 ご go" and ch3 "*〜ご . . . language" both reached the pool (chapter-1 ご "Five", chapter-2 ご "...language") and soundDeck.js kept the first. Downgraded to polish: unlike さん, the suffix sense only ever appears inside a word the deck cards whole (にほんご), so the learner never reads ご "language" on its own.

claim: せき carries only "Cough", though the book also prints せき "seat" in the RW1 long-vowel pairs that the deck already draws しゅじん and しゅうじん from.
evidence: Book ch14 Lesson 12: "せき cough". Book ch15 RW1: "5. せいき (century) — せき (seat)" beside "3. しゅじん (husband) — しゅうじん (prisoner)". Card r-29c26602d23e: せき "Cough".
fix: Make the English "Cough; seat", or leave it if the RW1 pairs are not meant to teach meanings (then reconsider しゅうじん too).
verdictReason: せき "seat" appears in the book only inside RW1's long-vowel pronunciation pairs (ch15, exercise E), and rule 1 says a word that only appears in an exercise is not taught; the Lesson 12 vocabulary (ch14) teaches せき "cough" and the card is faithful to it. The "seat" sense has its own card in the collection as the kanji word 席 (chapter-11, r-5c0dfdc8ee1d "Seat"). That しゅうじん got a card from the same drill is a separate question the finding does not raise.

claim: The target drops the お the book brackets, against the deck's own fullest-form convention.
evidence: Book ch23 Useful Expressions: "(お)たんじょうびおめでとう。(Happy Birthday)". The deck turns おやすみ(なさい) into おやすみなさい and ごちそうさま(でした) into ごちそうさまでした. Card r-f76f81e7a0e6: たんじょうびおめでとう.
fix: Change the target to おたんじょうびおめでとう (romaji otanjōbi omedetō).
verdictReason: Book ch23 Useful Expressions prints "(お)たんじょうびおめでとう。(Happy Birthday)". Rule 2 cards the fullest written form the book prints, and this deck already does so for every other bracketed part: おやすみ(なさい), おかえり(なさい), ごちそうさま(でした) and 〜おめでとう(ございます) ship as おやすみなさい, おかえりなさい, ごちそうさまでした, おめでとうございます. The pool entry (chapter-22 reading-report) already lacked the お, so the drop happened at the reader pass. No おたんじょうびおめでとう card elsewhere. Target change means new audio.

claim: きれい is carded without the な the book prints, while every other な-adjective in the kana deck carries it. The Learner saw the same thing from the other side: without な it files with the い-adjectives いい and かゆい.
evidence: Book ch7 Lesson 5 vocabulary: "きれい（な） beautiful; clean", and drills print きれいな. Cards: げんきな, ひまな, しずかな, にぎやかな, たいへんな all with な; r-2b8c515b4475 is きれい. Learner: Reading front 'きれい', back 'Answer: Beautiful; clean'. Compare 'げんきな', 'ひまな', 'しずかな', 'たいへんな', 'にぎやかな' on this unit, and 'いい' / 'かゆい' which end in い with no な.
fix: Change the target to きれいな (romaji kirei na). (The Learner's alternative, a note, is not available: a reading card has no note field.)
verdictReason: Book ch7 Lesson 5 vocabulary prints "きれい（な） beautiful; clean" beside げんき（な）, しずか（な）, にぎやか（な）, ひま（な）, and the drills print きれいな. The pool held both forms (chapter-6 reading-report: きれい AND きれいな; chapter-8: きれい); soundDeck.js took きれい first in book order and then dropped きれいな as "the hiragana budget was already full". Every other な-adjective in the deck carries な, and the owner excluded bare にぎやか on 2026-10-14 as a repeat of にぎやかな, which is the same choice. No other きれい or きれいな card in the collection, so the rename collides with nothing. Romaji becomes "kirei na" like "genki na"; new audio.
